subject: Runbook: latency-critical burst reservations for EdgePilot pilot
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: dev_patel@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: sarah.kline@edgepilot.ai
Date: 2027-04-22T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Runbook: latency-critical burst reservations for EdgePilot pilot

Team —

We have a time-boxed pilot with EdgePilot next month and they asked for a 1-week burst reservation to hit strict latency targets for a production-like load. I want to capture the runbook and get internal alignment on constraints, approvals, and tickets so we can move quickly if we approve. High level:

- Customer: EdgePilot (contact: sarah.kline@edgepilot.ai)
- Pilot window requested: 2027-05-03 00:00 UTC — 2027-05-10 00:00 UTC
- SLA ask for pilot: p95 generation latency < 50ms for short prompts at expected QPS (~150 concurrent streams across 3 US regions)
- Models: customer will use rdl-7b-quantized (primary) and rdl-3b-fallback (cheap)

Questions / asks:
1) Dev infra (Dev) — Feasibility: can we provision a one-week burst reservation that ensures cold-starts and KV-cache warmups won't violate p95? What autoscale overrides and pre-warm steps do you need from us?
2) Capacity (Karthik) — Do we have a safely carved pool or burst lane we can allocate without regressing other enterprise pilots? How much dedicated GPU equivalence should we request?
3) Sales/Customer (Laura) — Confirm EdgePilot is willing to accept overage billing for a short reservation and provide PO/billing contact. Also need the acceptance criteria and exact QPS schedule per region.
4) Product (me) — I can scope the rollout steps and experiments, and I want to include an automated fallback rule that routes to rdl-3b when p95 > 120ms for >2 minutes.

I've attached a filled burst_reservation_template.xlsx with the customer's requested schedule and rough QPS breakdown. Please reply with: a short bulleted list of blockers, the minimum GPU count you recommend, and whether you need a JIRA/INF ticket (and with what priority) to start provisioning.

Goal: have a go/no-go decision and ticket created by EOD 2027-04-22 so we can lock procurement and infra lead times.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Principal Product Manager, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai
Redwood Inference

Attachments: burst_reservation_template.xlsx
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: sarah.kline@edgepilot.ai
Date: 2027-04-22T10:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Runbook: latency-critical burst reservations for EdgePilot pilot

Marcus —

Thanks for the clear summary. Quick answers from infra ops:

- Feasibility: Yes, we can support a 1-week burst reservation, but it requires a few commitments to make the p95 target realistic. Main constraints: multi-tenant pool fragmentation and scheduler cooldown windows.

- Minimum request: For the stated QPS (~150 concurrent streams across 3 regions) and rdl-7b-quantized, I recommend reserving the equivalent of 8 A100-80GB GPUs (we'll map this to our pooled infra as 8-slot carveout) plus 2 extra for pre-warm/health.

- Autoscale & warmup: We'll need an autoscale override that disables aggressive downscale during the pilot window (set min_replicas to match the reserved units) and a pre-warm job that runs KV-cache priming for the top 20 prefixes. Expect ~45–60 minutes of warmup per region.

- Scheduler/tickets: Create an INF ticket with high priority and include: exact UTC window, the pool id (if you have a preference), and a billing code. We'll also need an owner for the pre-warm job and a test harness endpoint so we can verify p95 before turning customer traffic on.

- Operational caveats: If other enterprise pilots have overlapping windows, we may need to negotiate a time shift or split by region. Also, cold restarts due to driver upgrades within that week would cause missed SLA; we can set an override to postpone upgrades for the window.

I've attached our current gpu-pool-map.png showing candidate pools and latency baselines.

Next step: Marcus/Laura please confirm which pool (us-west-2-priority or us-east-1-burst) you prefer. If no preference, we will default to us-west-2-priority. I'll start a draft INF ticket once you confirm.

—Dev Patel
Infra Lead, Serving Runtime
dev_patel@redwood.ai

Attachments: gpu-pool-map.png
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, dev_patel@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: sarah.kline@edgepilot.ai, accounts@edgepilot.ai
Date: 2027-04-22T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Runbook: latency-critical burst reservations for EdgePilot pilot

Folks —

EdgePilot confirms they will accept short-term overage billing for the pilot and have provided a PO contact (accounts@edgepilot.ai). They also sent an SLA doc and regional traffic split: 60% us-west, 30% us-east, 10% us-central. Their engineering lead (Sarah) asked that we prioritize us-west for warmup.

Customer acceptance criteria for the pilot (copied from their doc):
- p95 end-to-end generation latency < 50ms for approved prompts
- No more than 1% error rate for model responses
- Demo window: 2027-05-05 15:00–16:00 UTC (customer-facing) — ideally fully warmed and validated 2 hours prior

I'll attach the SLA notes (edgepilot-sla-notes.pdf) and will push the PO once we have an INF ticket with a cost estimate. Marcus — can you confirm the demo window will be included in the reserved time? If so, I recommend we pick us-west-2-priority as the default pool so we can concentrate warmup there.

Laura Bennett
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai

Attachments: edgepilot-sla-notes.pdf
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, dev_patel@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-22T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Runbook: latency-critical burst reservations for EdgePilot pilot

Thanks — good thread. I'm fine approving a provisional burst reservation with the following conditions:

1) Ticket: Create INF-7421 with priority P1 and include the exact UTC window and billing code. Capacity team will only act on the ticket.
2) Capacity sizing: Approve 8 GPU-equivalent slots + 2 warmers as Dev recommended. If actual production traffic exceeds target by >20% for more than 30 minutes, auto-fallback to rdl-3b must be enabled.
3) No overlapping reserve: Confirm no other P1 reservations in us-west-2-priority during the window; infra to verify.
4) Billing: EdgePilot PO or explicit overage approval must be attached to INF-7421 before we spin up final reserved capacity.
5) Runbook & validation: Dev to provide a pre-warm checklist and a smoke-test endpoint. Product (Marcus) to confirm demo readiness 24 hours before the demo window.

I'll schedule a 30-minute sync for tomorrow 2027-04-23 10:00 PDT to finalize the ticket metadata and owners. After INF-7421 is created I'll assign an owner from capacity on the ticket and track provisioning SLA.

Karthik Iyer
Capacity Planning Manager, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

Related JIRA: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-7421
